segments.line: Nine am.. Rule one. You run everywhere.
For about ten seconds, it's amazing. You're flying past people, past dogs, past a guy on a scooter.
Then your legs turn to jelly.
That's real. Your muscles burn through their fastest fuel in about ten seconds of all out sprinting. After that, you slow down, whether you want to or not.
In the game, you'd run all day. In real life, you're bent over outside a pharmacy, wheezing, while the guy on the scooter rolls past and waves.
Ten am.. Rule two. Mo rents two electric scooters,
and you ride them like it's a car chase. Through the park, between the benches, around one very confused pigeon.
A park ranger blows a whistle.
You don't stop. Because in the game, you never stop.
Eleven am.. Rule four. You take a shortcut.
Over a fence, through a backyard, past a very surprised man in a bathrobe holding his morning coffee. Morning! you say.
He does not say morning back.
But his dog says a lot. The dog chases you all the way to the next fence, and you climb it a lot faster than the first one.
Noon. Rule three. You're hungry, you're scraped up, and your knee hurts from the fence.
So you heal, just like the game. Six hot dogs from the cart outside the station.
In the game, your health bar fills right back up.
In real life, six hot dogs with buns is around eighteen hundred calories, and it doesn't heal a single scrape.
Your stomach is very, very upset with you.
Twelve thirty. In the game, you'd walk into a clothing store and walk out in a new outfit, so nobody recognizes you.
So you try. Seven outfits in five minutes. A sombrero. A tracksuit. A suit that's three sizes too big.
The security guard watches every single change.
You leave in your own clothes. Minus the hoodie.
And the whole time, Mo is filming. And posting.
That's the part you forgot about.
